MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (this "Agreement"), dated as of March 14, 2025, is entered into by and between Meridian Analytics LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Provider"), and Corvus Freight Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Client"). This execution copy supersedes all prior drafts and term sheets exchanged between the parties.

1. Services; Non-Exclusive Relationship. Provider shall perform the data-engineering and freight-network analytics services described in mutually executed Statements of Work ("SOWs"). This Agreement is strictly non-exclusive: nothing herein restricts Client from engaging any other provider of similar services, or Provider from serving any other customer, including competitors of Client. Neither party makes any exclusive dealing commitment.

2. Fees. Fees are as stated in each SOW. Client has no minimum purchase, spend, or volume obligation under this Agreement. No most-favored-customer or most-favored-nation pricing commitment is made by either party.

3. Work Product; Assignment of Intellectual Property. All deliverables, reports, and models first created by Provider under an SOW ("Work Product") shall be the sole property of Client. Provider hereby irrevocably assigns to Client all right, title, and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in the Work Product, effective upon payment of the applicable fees.

4. Non-Solicitation of Personnel. During the term and for twelve (12) months after expiration or termination, neither party shall directly solicit for employment any employee or contractor of the other party who was materially involved in the Services. General public job postings are not a breach.

5. Insurance. Provider shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and cyber liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 in the aggregate, naming Client as an additional insured, with certificates delivered on request.

6. Audit Rights. Client may, on fifteen (15) days' written notice and not more than once in any twelve-month period, audit Provider's books and records related to invoiced fees and compliance with Sections 3 and 9, during normal business hours.

7. Term; Termination for Convenience. This Agreement continues until terminated. Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW for convenience, without cause and without penalty, upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice.

8. Post-Termination Transition Services. For ninety (90) days after any expiration or termination, Provider shall provide transition assistance, including data export in industry-standard formats and knowledge-transfer sessions, at the rates in the most recent SOW.

9. Limitation of Liability. EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN THE NEXT SENTENCE, EACH PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CLIENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM. THE CAP SHALL NOT APPLY TO PROVIDER'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS OR TO PROVIDER'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INFRINGEMENT INDEMNITY, AS TO WHICH PROVIDER'S LIABILITY IS UNCAPPED AND UNLIMITED. No liquidated damages or termination fees are payable under this Agreement.

10. Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of the other party. A change of control of a party (including by merger or sale of stock) shall NOT be deemed an assignment, shall require no consent or notice, and shall give the other party no termination right.

11. Warranty. Provider warrants only that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner. No warranty period of any specific duration is stated.

12. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles.

MERIDIAN ANALYTICS LLC — /s/ Dana Whitlock, Managing Member
CORVUS FREIGHT HOLDINGS, INC. — /s/ Emil Reyes, Chief Procurement Officer

GRIDCORE SOFTWARE LICENSE AGREEMENT (EXECUTION COPY)

This Software License Agreement (this "Agreement"), dated as of June 2, 2025, is entered into by and between Helix Grid, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Licensor"), and Tessellate Systems Ltd, a private limited company organized under the laws of England and Wales ("Licensee"). This execution copy supersedes in its entirety the superseded draft v2 dated April 18, 2025, and all other prior drafts.

1. Definitions. "Software" means Licensor's GridCore optimization engine, version 5.x, in object code form, together with its documentation. "Field" means maritime logistics scheduling and port-call optimization. "Net Revenue" means Licensee's gross revenue from Licensee products embedding the Software, less returns and taxes.

2. License Grant; Exclusivity. Licensor hereby grants to Licensee a perpetual and irrevocable license to use, reproduce, and distribute the Software solely within the Field. The license granted under this Section 2 is personal to Licensee and is non-transferable and non-sublicensable: Licensee may not assign, transfer, or sublicense the license, in whole or in part, to any third party without Licensor's prior written consent. During the term, Licensor shall not license, sell, or otherwise make the Software available to any person other than Licensee for use within the Field; this exclusive dealing commitment is a material inducement to Licensee's execution of this Agreement.

3. Royalties; Revenue Sharing. In consideration of the license, Licensee shall pay Licensor a running royalty equal to four percent (4%) of Net Revenue, payable within forty-five (45) days after the end of each calendar quarter. There is no minimum royalty and no minimum purchase, order, or usage commitment of any kind under this Agreement, and no volume-based fee increase or usage threshold applies.

4. Most Favored Licensee. If, during the term, Licensor grants any third party a license to the Software on royalty rates or fee terms more favorable than those set forth in Section 3, Licensor shall notify Licensee within thirty (30) days, and such more favorable terms shall automatically be extended to Licensee, retroactive to the effective date of the third-party grant.

5. Source Code Escrow. Within thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, Licensor shall deposit the source code of the Software with Iron Vault Fiduciary Services LLC pursuant to a three-party escrow agreement. The deposit shall be updated with each major release and shall be released to Licensee upon Licensor's bankruptcy, insolvency, general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or cessation of business operations.

6. Limited Warranty. Licensor warrants that, for a period of twelve (12) months following initial delivery, the Software will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Licensee's exclusive remedy for breach of this warranty is repair, replacement, or, if neither is commercially practicable, refund of royalties paid for the affected period.

7. Covenant Not to Sue; No Challenge. Licensee covenants that it shall not, during the term and for three (3) years thereafter, bring or voluntarily assist any action contesting the validity, enforceability, or Licensor's ownership of any patent, copyright, or trade secret embodied in the Software.

8. Term; Termination. This Agreement continues in perpetuity unless terminated by a party for a material breach that remains uncured sixty (60) days after written notice. Neither party has any right to terminate this Agreement for convenience or without cause. The license granted in Section 2, being irrevocable, survives any termination other than termination by Licensor for Licensee's uncured payment breach.

9. Insurance. For the avoidance of doubt, neither party is required by this Agreement to obtain or maintain any insurance for the benefit of the other party.

10. Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflicts-of-law rules.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
HELIX GRID, INC. — /s/ Priya Raman, Chief Executive Officer
TESSELLATE SYSTEMS LTD — /s/ Callum Firth, Director

SUPPLY AGREEMENT (EXECUTION COPY)

This Supply Agreement (this "Agreement"), dated as of September 9, 2025, is entered into by and between Bluewater Components LLC, a Michigan limited liability company ("Supplier"), and Argent Motors Corporation, a Nevada corporation ("Buyer").

1. Scope. Supplier shall manufacture and sell to Buyer electro-hydraulic brake actuators, part number family BA-7 (the "Products"), conforming to the specifications in Exhibit A.

2. Minimum Purchase Commitment. Buyer shall purchase not fewer than forty thousand (40,000) units of Products in each Contract Year. If Buyer's purchases fall short of the minimum in any Contract Year, Buyer shall pay Supplier a true-up equal to sixty percent (60%) of the then-current unit price for each unit of shortfall.

3. Forecasts; Volume Threshold. Buyer shall deliver rolling quarterly forecasts, the first month of which is binding. Purchase orders in any quarter exceeding one hundred twenty percent (120%) of the binding forecast require Supplier's prior written consent and are subject to a six percent (6%) expedite surcharge on the excess units.

4. Pricing; Price Restrictions. Unit prices in Exhibit B are firm for the first twenty-four (24) months of the term. Thereafter, Supplier may adjust unit prices no more than once per Contract Year and by no more than the lesser of (a) the percentage change in the Producer Price Index for motor vehicle parts and (b) three percent (3%). Except as expressly stated in this Section 4, Supplier may not increase or decrease prices. No most-favored-customer or most-favored-nation pricing commitment is made under this Agreement.

5. Non-Compete. During the term and for two (2) years following its expiration or termination, Supplier shall not develop, manufacture, or supply brake actuators functionally equivalent to the Products for any passenger-vehicle original equipment manufacturer in North America other than Buyer.

6. Non-Solicitation of Customers. During the term and for one (1) year thereafter, Supplier shall not solicit any member of Buyer's franchised dealer network for direct aftermarket sales of the Products or functionally equivalent goods.

7. Right of First Refusal. Before selling, licensing, or otherwise transferring the BA-7 product line, its tooling, or related manufacturing assets to any third party, Supplier shall first offer such sale or transfer to Buyer on terms no less favorable than those offered to the third party. Buyer shall have forty-five (45) days from receipt of the offer to accept.

8. Change of Control. If Supplier undergoes a change of control — including a merger, sale of a majority of its equity, or a sale of all or substantially all of its assets — Supplier shall give Buyer prompt written notice, and Buyer may terminate this Agreement upon written notice delivered within ninety (90) days after receiving Supplier's notice.

9. Late Delivery; Liquidated Damages. For any shipment delivered more than five (5) business days after the confirmed delivery date, Supplier shall pay Buyer liquidated damages of seventy-five dollars ($75) per unit per week of delay, capped at ten percent (10%) of the value of the affected order. The parties agree this sum is a genuine pre-estimate of Buyer's loss and not a penalty.

10. Insurance. Supplier shall maintain product liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence with an insurer rated A- or better, naming Buyer as an additional insured, and shall furnish certificates of insurance annually.

11. Third-Party Beneficiaries. Buyer's affiliates that purchase Products under this Agreement are express and intended third-party beneficiaries of Sections 9 and 10 and may enforce those Sections directly against Supplier.

12. Books and Records. Supplier shall maintain quality records for seven (7) years. Buyer shall have NO right under this Agreement to audit Supplier's books, records, or facilities; Supplier's compliance is verified solely through part-submission warrants and certificates of conformance. Each party's liability under this Agreement is subject to the remedies expressly stated herein.

13. Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.
BLUEWATER COMPONENTS LLC — /s/ Marta Okafor, President
ARGENT MOTORS CORPORATION — /s/ Theo Lindqvist, VP Global Purchasing

EMAIL THREAD — MSA NEGOTIATION FILE (Meridian Analytics / Corvus Freight)

From: Emil Reyes (Corvus Freight, CPO)  To: Dana Whitlock (Meridian Analytics)
Date: February 20, 2025  Subject: RE: MSA open points

Dana — three asks from our side before signature: (1) most-favored-nation pricing: Corvus should automatically receive any better rate Meridian gives another freight customer; (2) exclusivity: Meridian should work only with Corvus in the freight-brokerage vertical for the term; (3) a liquidated damages schedule for missed SOW milestones.

From: Dana Whitlock (Meridian Analytics)  To: Emil Reyes (Corvus Freight)
Date: February 24, 2025  Subject: RE: RE: MSA open points

Emil — we can't accept any of the three. Our rate card varies with scope, so an MFN commitment is off the table. Exclusivity in the freight vertical would gut our pipeline; the agreement will state expressly that the relationship is non-exclusive. And we don't do liquidated damages in services agreements — the liability section will instead cap general damages at trailing twelve-month fees, with the cap lifted for confidentiality and IP-indemnity breaches. What we CAN offer: the 60-day convenience termination right you asked for, the 90-day transition assistance package, the annual audit right, and the $2M CGL / $5M cyber insurance certificates.

From: Emil Reyes  Date: February 25, 2025
Accepted. Drop MFN, exclusivity, and the LD schedule; keep the rest as you describe. Legal will paper it — signature copy to follow in March.

[Negotiation-file note, March 17, 2025: The executed MSA of March 14, 2025 reflects the February 25 compromise. No MFN clause, no exclusivity clause, and no liquidated damages clause appear in the executed agreement. This thread is retained for context only and has no contractual effect.]

NON-BINDING TERM SHEET — ACTUATOR SUPPLY PROGRAM (Bluewater Components / Argent Motors)
Dated July 1, 2025 — FOR DISCUSSION PURPOSES ONLY

This term sheet summarizes preliminary positions for a proposed supply agreement for BA-7 brake actuators. Except for the confidentiality paragraph, this term sheet is NON-BINDING and creates no obligations. The definitive Supply Agreement, once executed, will alone govern.

Proposed terms (Argent draft positions):
- Volume: Argent to commit to a minimum of 40,000 units per year (carried into definitive agreement).
- Pricing: firm 24 months, then index-capped adjustments (carried into definitive agreement).
- AUDIT RIGHTS (proposed): Argent proposed a right to audit Bluewater's books, quality records, and plants twice per year with 10 days' notice. [Status note, September 12, 2025: REJECTED by Bluewater during definitive drafting. The executed Supply Agreement of September 9, 2025 expressly provides that Argent has no audit right and relies on certificates of conformance instead.]
- MOST FAVORED NATION (proposed): Argent proposed that if Bluewater sells equivalent actuators to any other OEM at a lower unit price, Argent receives that price retroactively. [Status note: DROPPED in definitive drafting; the executed Supply Agreement states that no most-favored-customer commitment is made.]
- Uncapped liability (proposed): Argent proposed uncapped supplier liability for recalls. [Status note: not adopted as drafted; the definitive agreement instead uses the liquidated-damages schedule and insurance requirements.]

Bluewater counter-positions accepted into the definitive agreement: change-of-control termination right for Argent, right of first refusal over the BA-7 line, dealer-network non-solicitation, two-year OEM non-compete, $5M product liability insurance, affiliate third-party-beneficiary language, Texas governing law.

Reminder to the deal team: clause extraction and evidence filings must be based on the executed Supply Agreement, not on this term sheet.
